also: can you show me the way?
could you show me the way?

terms.grammar: mōnstrō with the dative of the person: mihi viam mōnstrā
evidence: Enn. ap. Cic. Off. 1.51: homō, quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrat viam
Plaut. Rud. 212: aut viam aut sēmitam mōnstret
Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1.132: quī sibi sēmitam nōn sapiunt, alterī mōnstrant viam
terms.comment: The old phrase, from Ennius and Plautus. mōnstrāre alone shows where a person or a place is: Sciō ubi sit, vērum hodiē numquam mōnstrābō (Ter. Ad. 570).

terms.gloss: point out (the way, where someone lives); give directions
evidence: Ter. Ph. 306: aut ubi habitet dēmōnstrārier
terms.comment: Pointing out the way in words, as one gives directions: Livy’s praetor sets out the routes for the envoys with care.

phrases.latin: homō, quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrat viam, quasi lūmen dē suō lūmine accendat, facit. nihilō minus ipsī lūcet, cum illī accenderit
phrases.english: the man who kindly shows a lost traveller the way acts as if he lit another’s lamp from his own: it shines no less for him once he has lit the other’s

phrases.latin: saltem aliquem velim quī mihi ex hīs locīs aut viam aut sēmitam mōnstret
phrases.english: I wish at least there were someone to show me a road or a path out of this place

phrases.latin: Quō vīs īre? Viam tibi libenter ostendam.
phrases.english: Where do you want to go? I’ll gladly show you the way.

phrases.latin: Mōnstrā mihi, sīs, quā ad forum ītur.
phrases.english: Show me, would you, which way it is to the square.

phrases.latin: Dat quī prōsequantur; itinera cum cūrā dēmōnstrat
phrases.english: He gives them men to escort them, and carefully sets out the routes for them

sources: Lewis & Short: monstro · Lewis & Short: ostendo · Lewis & Short: demonstro
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 172.
